ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that $\triangle ABC$ is an equilateral triangle with a side length of 6, and point D is on side $BC$ with $BD=2$. Construct an equilateral triangle $ADE$ with $AD$ as its side. Through point E, draw $EF\parallel BC$ intersecting $AC$ at point F. Connect $BF$. What is the area $S_{\text{quadrilateral }BDEF}$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Draw $EC$, and construct $CH\perp EF$ at $H$,\\
since $\triangle ABC$ and $\triangle ADE$ are both equilateral triangles,\\
therefore $AB=AC$, $AD=AE$, $\angle BAC=\angle DAE=\angle ABC=\angle ACB=60^\circ$,\\
thus $\angle BAD=\angle CAE$,\\
in $\triangle BAD$ and $\triangle CAE$,\\
$\left\{\begin{array}{l}
AB=AC\\
\angle BAD=\angle CAE\\
AD=AE
\end{array}\right.$,\\
thus $\triangle BAD \cong \triangle CAE(SAS)$,\\
thus $BD=EC=2$, $\angle ACE=\angle ABD=60^\circ$,\\
since $EF\parallel BC$,\\
thus $\angle EFC=\angle ACB=60^\circ$,\\
thus $\triangle EFC$ is an equilateral triangle,\\
therefore $CH=\sqrt{3}$, $EF=EC=BD=2$,\\
since $EF\parallel BD$,\\
thus quadrilateral $BDEF$ is a parallelogram,\\
thus the area of quadrilateral $BDEF=BD\cdot CH=2\sqrt{3}$.\\
Hence, the answer is: $S_{\text{quadrilateral}BDEF}=\boxed{2\sqrt{3}}$.

raw_record.original_question: In the figure, $\triangle ABC$ is an equilateral triangle with side length 6, and point $D$ is on side $BC$ with $BD=2$. Construct an equilateral triangle $ADE$ with $AD$ as a side. Through point $E$, draw $EF\parallel BC$ intersecting $AC$ at point $F$. Connect $BF$. Find the area $S_{\text{quadrilateral }BDEF}$.
raw_record.answer: Draw $EC$, and construct $CH\perp EF$ at $H$. Since $\triangle ABC$ and $\triangle ADE$ are both equilateral triangles, $AB=AC$, $AD=AE$, and $\angle BAC=\angle DAE=\angle ABC=\angle ACB=60^\circ$. Thus $\angle BAD=\angle CAE$. In $\triangle BAD$ and $\triangle CAE$, $AB=AC$, $\angle BAD=\angle CAE$, and $AD=AE$, so $\triangle BAD \cong \triangle CAE$ (SAS). Therefore $BD=EC=2$, and $\angle ACE=\angle ABD=60^\circ$. Since $EF\parallel BC$, $\angle EFC=\angle ACB=60^\circ$, so $\triangle EFC$ is an equilateral triangle. Hence $CH=\sqrt{3}$ and $EF=EC=BD=2$. Since $EF\parallel BD$, quadrilateral $BDEF$ is a parallelogram. Therefore, the area of quadrilateral $BDEF$ is $BD\cdot CH=2\sqrt{3}$. Hence, $S_{\text{quadrilateral }BDEF}=\boxed{2\sqrt{3}}$.
raw_record.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, A is the upper vertex, B and C are below forming the base of triangle ABC, and D is on BC and close to B. Segments AD and AE form equilateral triangle ADE, with E located outside on the right side of AC. EF drawn through E is parallel to BC and intersects AC at F; BF is also connected in the figure, and the area of quadrilateral BDEF is required. Reasoning: Because ABC and ADE are both equilateral triangles, AB=AC, AD=AE, and ∠BAC=∠DAE=60°. Subtracting the two 60° angles gives ∠BAD=∠CAE. Thus in triangles BAD and CAE, AB=AC, AD=AE, and the included angle ∠BAD=∠CAE, so the two are congruent by SAS. Therefore EC=BD=2, and ∠ACE=∠ABD=60°. Also because EF∥BC, and F is on AC, ∠EFC=∠ACB=60°; at the same time ∠ECF=∠ECA=60°. Therefore triangle EFC is an equilateral triangle, and EF=EC=2. The side length of equilateral triangle EFC is 2, and its height is 2·√3/2=√3, which is also the distance between the parallel lines EF and BC. Since BD∥EF and BD=EF=2, quadrilateral BDEF is a parallelogram, and its area is base BD times height, namely 2·√3=2√3.
